semantic_rejection_rule: Reject URL-new candidates if the feature/mechanism or transaction is substantially equivalent to any in-window record; compare workflow, failure, evidence, remediation, question and diagram fingerprints.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: BGP TCP Authentication Option (TCP-AO): key-chain binding, algorithm selection, and authenticated peer transport
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: TCP-AO authenticates BGP's TCP transport with key-chain selected per neighbor/neighbor-group; AES-128-CMAC or HMAC-SHA1 algorithm, send/receive key identifiers and validity windows; distinct from route policy and legacy TCP MD5.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure key-chain and key ID on both peers -> select key-chain using BGP neighbor auth-options -> TCP-AO option/key negotiation authenticates SYN/segments -> BGP OPEN/KEEPALIVE/UPDATE exchange proceeds only after transport authentication.
selected_candidates.failure_class: BGP peer remains Active/Idle or resets because peer key-chain, key ID, algorithm, send/receive key lifetime or neighbor binding differs.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys tcp-auth-options shows peer address, algorithm, send-id/recv-id, flags and send/receive validity windows; BGP summary and TCP/session debug establish whether transport authentication or BGP capability negotiation failed.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Align key-chain name, key ID, algorithm and active validity window on both peers; verify neighbor or neighbor-group binding; stage overlapping keys for rollover where supported; confirm TCP-AO state before changing BGP timers or route policy.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A BGP peer is reachable by ping but TCP establishment fails after TCP-AO rollout; distinguish transport-auth mismatch from BGP UPDATE or route-map failure.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two FortiGate BGP peers with parallel key-chain/key-ID/algorithm objects above TCP-AO authenticated transport, then BGP FSM and route exchange; failure branch before OPEN.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiManager 8.0 time-based retention for Task Monitor and Event Log: log-max-days versus disk-quota retention
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager local task-monitor and event-log retention can be bounded by log age with system local log disk setting log-max-days 0..365; zero restores disk-quota-driven retention.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Administrator sets local retention days -> FortiManager evaluates local Task Monitor/Event Log records -> at midnight records older than configured age are truncated; zero delegates retention back to disk quota.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Expected task/install history disappears earlier than operators expect, or disk pressure remains because age-based and quota-based retention assumptions are confused.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: CLI configuration read-back for log-max-days, Task Monitor/Event Log oldest timestamps, and disk/log quota state; age cutoff appears after midnight.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Choose a retention horizon that meets audit and troubleshooting requirements; retain exports before shortening the window; use zero only when quota-based behavior is intended; verify after the midnight truncation cycle.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Task history older than five days disappears after the nightly cleanup despite unused disk quota; identify the age-based retention control.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager local event/task log store feeding an age evaluator and midnight purge boundary, with disk quota fallback when log-max-days equals zero.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Authenticated NTPv4 with SHA-256: Chrony key-file alignment, key IDs, and time-service verification
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer NTP client supports NTPv4 symmetric-key SHA-256 authentication with ASCII or hex key material and key ID matched to Chrony server key file; this authenticates time messages rather than encrypting the time payload.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Chrony server loads chrony.conf and chrony.keys -> FortiAnalyzer NTP server object points to server and matching key ID/key format/key -> authenticated NTP exchanges establish time synchronization -> diagnose system ntp status reports state.
selected_candidates.failure_class: NTP server is reachable but authenticated synchronization fails because key ID, key format, secret bytes, authentication enablement or Chrony key-file configuration differs.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose system ntp status, FortiAnalyzer config system ntp ntpserver read-back, Chrony configuration and key-file entry; UDP reachability alone does not prove MAC authentication succeeded.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Match key ID and exact key bytes; choose hex or ASCII consistently; enable authentication and SHA-256 on FortiAnalyzer; ensure Chrony keyfile is active and server ACL permits the appliance; rotate keys in a coordinated window.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: NTP packets reach Chrony but FortiAnalyzer does not synchronize after SHA-256 is enabled; find the key-ID/key-format boundary.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer NTP client and Linux Chrony server with matching key ID and SHA-256 key objects, UDP time exchange and authentication decision; mismatched key branch rejected.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiSwitch IP conflict detection: passive ARP ownership claims, active gratuitous-ARP probes, logs, and SNMP traps
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Global IP conflict detection uses two ARP observations: passive broadcast ARP claims matching a FortiSwitch system-interface IP, and active gratuitous ARP probes on boot/interface-up/IP-change; conflict creates system log and SNMP trap.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable global detect-ip-conflict -> switch observes ARP claim or emits gratuitous ARP after qualifying event -> conflicting owner replies or claims same interface IP -> switch records conflict and raises SNMP trap.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Duplicate address intermittently disrupts switch management or routing, but operators assume the feature scans every endpoint or mistake a silent host-to-host duplicate for a monitored system-interface collision.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: System event log with interface/IP conflict, SNMP trap, packet capture of ARP claim or gratuitous-ARP probe/reply; absence of a log does not prove no duplicate exists elsewhere in the VLAN.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Identify the conflicting MAC and interface; correct static addressing or DHCP scope overlap; verify global detection state and SNMP receiver; do not substitute this feature for DHCP snooping, DAI or an IPAM audit.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A duplicate IP is reported for a FortiSwitch management address; determine which ARP observation triggers the switch event and what address scope is actually covered.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch system interface and two endpoint MACs on a shared L2 segment; passive ARP claim and active gratuitous-ARP probe arrows converge on conflict log/SNMP trap.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Dynamic captive-portal URL from Cisco ISE: Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL in RADIUS Access-Accept
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Tunnel-mode captive-portal VAP with portal-type auth-mac can consume vendor-specific RADIUS attribute Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL (ID 27) from Cisco ISE Access-Accept when captive-portal-dynamic-redirect-url is enabled.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Station associates -> MAC RADIUS authentication places it in unregistered group -> ISE Access-Accept returns dynamic portal URL -> FortiGate redirects browser to session-specific portal -> user authentication changes station group to AuthorizedGuest and cp_authed becomes yes.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Wireless association and MAB succeed but client lands on wrong/default portal or never redirects because VAP mode/type or ISE authorization attribute is absent or malformed.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose wireless-controller wlac -d sta online shows group, rad_mac_auth and cp_authed; diagnose firewall auth list shows RADIUS server/group/session; captured Access-Accept confirms attribute 27.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use tunnel-mode captive portal with auth-mac; enable dynamic redirect; define Fortinet vendor attribute 27 in ISE dictionary and authorization profile; verify the returned URL and post-login group transition.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A client passes MAB but always receives the default portal despite an ISE authorization policy; locate the RADIUS attribute and VAP eligibility boundary.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wireless station -> FortiAP/FortiGate tunnel VAP -> RADIUS Access-Request to Cisco ISE -> Access-Accept carrying portal URL -> browser portal -> authorized group.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiNAC authentication-policy timers: production grace, offline authentication retention, and forced reauthentication
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Authentication policy binds one User/Host Profile to one authentication configuration; configuration carries time-in-production-before-authentication, time-offline-before-deauthentication and reauthentication-frequency timers; first matching policy wins.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Host/user/location evaluated against ordered authentication policies -> matched profile selects authentication configuration -> host remains in production during grace -> timeout moves host to authentication VLAN -> offline timer preserves prior auth for bounded reconnect -> periodic reauth can force authentication VLAN regardless of online state.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Endpoint remains in production too long, is unexpectedly forced to authentication VLAN after a brief disconnect, or never receives intended authentication configuration because catch-all/first-match policy shadows it.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Policy Details shows matched profile/configuration and policy assessment debug log; host connectivity and VLAN state over time; RADIUS success proves identity only, not the final NAC access policy.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Place catch-all profile last; set timers deliberately for endpoint class; verify first matching profile and selected configuration; separate external RADIUS authentication success from NAC VLAN decision.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A laptop reconnects within the offline retention interval but is challenged again; identify which timer and policy-match state govern the behavior.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Host/location inputs feed ordered User-Host Profile match list -> Authentication Configuration timer state machine -> production/authentication VLAN outcomes; separate RADIUS identity path.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiNAC-F 802.1X with Microsoft Entra ID using EAP-TTLS/PAP and the Local RADIUS TLS service
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F Local RADIUS terminates EAP-TTLS and carries PAP credentials inside the TLS tunnel; a Microsoft Entra ID service connector acts as the authentication source through registered application credentials; supplicant must use TTLS-PAP rather than PEAP.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Windows supplicant starts 802.1X -> switch forwards EAP to FortiNAC Local RADIUS -> EAP-TTLS TLS tunnel established with Local RADIUS certificate -> PAP inner credentials sent to Entra-backed authentication source -> Access-Accept and NAC policy determine registration/production VLAN.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Cloud Entra users fail on wireless/wired 802.1X although a basic connector test succeeds because the supplicant selects PEAP instead of TTLS, local RADIUS TLS prerequisites are incomplete, or the Entra service connector fails independently. Recent adjacent scenario: Entra group import can fail on a >255-character description; distinguish group sync from EAP authentication.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: RADIUS debug and Access-Accept/Reject, Windows supplicant EAP method, service connector Test/Poll logs, Local RADIUS TLS certificate and mapping; successful Entra connector test alone does not prove TTLS exchange.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Configure Local RADIUS TLS service; register Entra application and connector; create Entra ID mapping and attach it to virtual server; enable TTLS/PAP and set Windows supplicant to EAP-TTLS with PAP; remember TTLS-PAP Entra flow does not support MFA.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Entra credentials pass a connector test but Windows 802.1X immediately rejects; identify the EAP method mismatch before changing credentials.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Windows supplicant EAP-TTLS/PAP -> FortiSwitch/FortiGate authenticator -> FortiNAC-F Local RADIUS TLS termination -> Entra ID service connector -> Access-Accept and VLAN policy.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 TACACS+ client groups: reusable device cohorts and policy binding
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: TACACS+ client objects can be grouped and used as policy selectors alongside individual clients; client groups have their own REST API endpoints and do not replace per-client address/shared-secret identity.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Register TACACS+ clients -> create group from selected client objects -> create TACACS+ policy -> bind individual clients and/or groups -> request from registered client matches policy -> configured identity source/authentication/authorization response is applied.
selected_candidates.failure_class: A device is registered but its TACACS+ request does not match the expected policy because it is absent from the selected group, the group is not attached, client address/secret is wrong, or TACACS+ is disabled on the receiving interface.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Authentication > TACACS+ Service > Clients and Groups membership, policy chosen-client/group list, interface service enablement, /debug/ TACACS+ logs and API group-association records.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Verify client object and shared secret first; verify group membership and policy binding; ensure TACACS+ is enabled on the ingress interface; use group CRUD/association endpoints for controlled automation.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A newly added switch appears in the TACACS client list but authenticates against no policy; trace the group-membership and policy-binding relationship.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Three TACACS+ device client objects feed two reusable client groups; groups and individual clients converge on a TACACS+ policy and identity-source/authorization response.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiPAM approval email via Microsoft Graph: OAuth application, mailbox permission, and approval notification path
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 approval-email protocol can use Microsoft Graph with Entra enterprise application, tenant/app/user identifiers, client secret, Mail.ReadWrite permission and Exchange service-principal mailbox permission instead of traditional SMTP.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Approval request created in FortiPAM -> approval-email worker obtains Graph OAuth token -> Graph accesses configured Microsoft 365 mailbox under service-principal permission -> notification sent -> approver follows FortiPAM approval workflow; email transport does not grant secret access itself.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Approval workflow is created but email is not delivered because Graph permission/consent, mailbox assignment, service-principal registration, mailbox access or token/tenant/app identifiers are inconsistent.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiPAM approval-email CLI settings, Entra app permission/admin consent, Exchange service principal and mailbox FullAccess, token acquisition and Graph send result; a pending approval record does not prove email delivery.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use a dedicated mailbox and enterprise application; grant documented Graph permission and admin consent; create Exchange service principal and mailbox permission; configure exact tenant/app/user IDs and client secret; test notification and rotate secrets under change control.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Approval requests are pending but approvers receive no messages after SMTP was replaced; isolate Graph token, permission, and mailbox authorization layers.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM approval request -> Graph OAuth token service -> Microsoft Graph API -> dedicated M365 mailbox -> approver; separate approval-state engine remains in FortiPAM.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM Windows Agent certificate monitoring: store-level add/remove/expiry events and template distribution
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Windows Agent 7.1+ certificate monitoring is configured per Windows certificate store in a Windows Agent Monitor Template; Add/Delete/Expiring/Expired operations generate distinct AO-WUA-Certificate event types.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create monitor template -> select certificate stores and event/expiry thresholds -> associate template with host(s) -> Apply distributes monitoring policy -> Windows Agent observes store changes/expiry -> event transported to FortiSIEM and available for rules/reports.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Expected certificate events are absent or expiry alerts are early/late because template was not associated/applied, wrong store was selected, or event types/expiry thresholds were not enabled.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Host-to-template association and Apply state; event search for AO-WUA-Certificate-Added/Removed/Expired/Expiring; sample event timestamp/store/host; agent status and Collector ingestion.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Confirm supported Windows Agent version and host registration; configure the relevant certificate store and operations; associate and Apply template; verify raw event arrival before adjusting correlation rules.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A certificate is removed from LocalMachine but no FortiSIEM alert appears; identify the store-operation-template association and event ingestion stages.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSIEM Supervisor template -> Windows Agent on host -> certificate-store watcher -> four event types -> Collector/event database -> rule/report.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Agent-based ZTNA destination ranges and port lists: FortiClient private-application matching
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE Feature-version agent-based ZTNA private applications can represent destination as IP range or CIDR and port list/range, subject to FortiClient Windows 7.2.8+; app object binds to FortiGate ZTNA gateway and endpoint-profile connection rule.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create ZTNA application gateway -> define private application IP/FQDN/range/CIDR and ports -> bind gateway -> select application in endpoint-profile ZTNA connection rule -> FortiClient matches protected TCP destination and forwards through ZTNA gateway -> gateway policy authorizes application.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Some hosts or ports bypass/miss ZTNA because endpoint FortiClient version lacks range/port-list support, app object is not referenced by profile, gateway address/port is wrong, or policy does not admit destination.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiSASE application object Type/range/CIDR/ports, endpoint-profile connection rule, FortiClient version, gateway status and FortiGate ZTNA logs; an object existing in portal does not prove it is deployed to endpoint.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Confirm Feature-version instance and FortiClient Windows 7.2.8+; define precise ranges and ports; bind correct gateway; reference app in endpoint profile; verify FortiGate application policy and endpoint profile receipt.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A new subnet-based private application appears in FortiSASE but Windows endpoints still connect directly; identify client-version and endpoint-profile binding boundaries.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiClient endpoint profile with connection rule -> private-application range/CIDR and port matcher -> FortiGate ZTNA application gateway -> protected application subnet.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: SD-WAN member priority to BGP MED mapping: spoke overlay SLA state, hub route advertisement, and external path choice
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: On a spoke, config system sdwan neighbor maps selected overlay members and health-check to BGP route-metric; priority mode uses priority-in-sla/priority-out-sla values to set MED on routes advertised to hub, which then advertises relative metrics to external eBGP peers.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Spoke measures overlay SLA -> member priorities reflect in-SLA/out-of-SLA state -> SD-WAN neighbor route-metric derives MED for iBGP route advertisement -> hub exports spoke prefixes with MED -> external router compares eligible paths and chooses preferred hub.
selected_candidates.failure_class: External traffic uses unexpected hub because neighbor/member binding, health-check, priority-in-sla/out-sla or BGP MED propagation is misunderstood; healthy tunnel alone does not guarantee preferred route.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys sdwan health-check shows member SLA state and priorities; get router info bgp neighbors <peer> advertised-routes shows Metric/MED; compare both hubs and external router best path.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Bind intended members and health-check to each BGP neighbor; choose priority or preferable route-metric intentionally; configure SLA priorities; verify advertised MED at both hubs and external decision point; avoid confusing MED with local preference.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Two hubs both advertise the same spoke prefix but traffic uses the hub with higher SLA quality; inspect the member priority-to-MED mapping and external BGP metric.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Dual-hub SD-WAN spoke with two overlay members and SLA probes feeding priority-to-MED mapping; iBGP spoke-to-hubs, then eBGP hubs-to-external router with MED comparison.
